title: Good Because It Is Commanded, or Because It Is Good?
summary: An episode debating whether a thing's goodness stems from its having been commanded or from a value it carries in itself; Plato's dilemma in the Euthyphro is compared with the ḥusn–qubḥ debate in kalām (the Muʿtazila's claim that reason discovers the good, al-Ashʿarī's priority of the command, al-Māturīdī's middle path). By way of Dostoevsky's question of whether everything is permitted if God does not exist, Kant's autonomous morality, and Ibn Rushd's reconciliation of reason and revealed law, the question of whether a person who follows the rule is genuinely moral is taken up through everyday examples.
